_comment: The procurement layer added on 2026-10-22 on top of data/b2b.json: six product families, five industry pages, a capability (trust) page, an export-logistics page, a procurement FAQ, the quick enquiry and the French Africa hub.
Rendered by tools/build-modunera-v2.mjs (buildCatalog). English, plus fr_africa in French. No German twin yet: the pages carry no hreflang pair except en/africa <-> fr/afrique.

Honesty rules, the same as b2b.json: every family is status project_specific_concept — a web catalogue entry, not a certified, serially produced or delivered product. Technical rows carry a basis: 'reference' means the figure is MODUNERA's published tiny-house reference (2.55 m base width, steel frame, road/Ro-Ro/sea delivery); 'per_project' means the value is set by engineering for the project and is not published. No price, no certificate, no capacity, no delivered project, no client name.
The family codes (MOD-FP, MOD-PH ...) are catalogue codes for enquiries and internal routing, not product approvals.
Do not write 'own production' or 'own factory': data/blocked-claims.json blocks those phrases until evidence exists. Use 'built to MODUNERA's specification'.
status_label: Project-specific concept — subject to engineering and capacity confirmation

systems.h2: Which building system fits which job
systems.p: Four ways to deliver a modular building. Which one a project uses depends on transport, site access, the number of units and how permanent the building is meant to be — decided in the feasibility step, not here.
rows: Large numbers of identical rooms shipped in compact packs: site offices, dormitories, sanitary units, storage
Assembly on site needs a trained crew; finishes are simpler than a volumetric unit; local approval of the system is a project question
Single-storey houses and buildings with a freer plan: staff housing, rural and serial housing, schools
More site work than volumetric: foundations, panel erection, roofing and finishes on site
Units fitted out before they leave the hall: hospitality units, homes, clinics and offices where finish quality matters
Transport size and crane access set the limits; fewer units per truck or container
Single premium units for private living, holiday rental and small hospitality
A mobile unit and a permanent dwelling or hotel room are different permit categories in most countries

steps: Your programme, site, country, quantities and timeline.
Export, customs, permits, transport and partner questions for the destination.
Module types, counts and a schematic site arrangement.
Scope, exclusions, delivery terms and the open points.
Structure, building physics and services against the applicable local codes, by qualified engineers.
Built to MODUNERA's specification once drawings and specification are signed off.
Inspection points agreed in the contract.
Road, Ro-Ro or sea freight to the agreed delivery point.
By MODUNERA's team, a local partner or the client's contractor — as the contract sets out.

incoterms: Delivery terms (EXW, FCA, FOB, CIF, DAP or other) are agreed per project and per Incoterms edition in the contract. Nothing on this page fixes a delivery term, a price or a lead time.

families.title: Modular workforce camps for remote project sites | MODUNERA
families.description: Workforce accommodation, sanitation, dining and administration modules structured around crew size, shift pattern, site access and phased delivery. Compliance and capacity confirmed per project.
families.h1: Workforce accommodation for remote project sites.
families.lead: Modular accommodation, sanitation, dining and administration concepts structured around workforce capacity, site access and phased delivery. Final technical compliance and production capacity are confirmed for each project.
families.wa: Hello MODUNERA, I am planning a modular workforce camp in __ for approximately __ people. Shift pattern: __. Target date: __.
who_for: Mining and energy operators housing crews on sites far from towns
EPC and main contractors mobilising a project workforce
Infrastructure programmes with phased crews over several years
use_cases: A 100-person exploration or construction camp with rooms, sanitary block, dining and a site office
A camp that grows from a first phase to 300 or more beds as the project ramps up
A management compound with single rooms, offices and a meeting space inside a larger camp
tech: Flat-pack, panelised or volumetric, chosen per camp
2.55 m base width for road-legal volumetric units
Single, twin or dormitory rooms, with or without en-suite
Specified for the site's climate zone
To the applicable local code, verified by a local engineer
Pads, strip or screw piles, by site investigation
Grid, generator or off-grid, assessed per site
configurations: Accommodation blocks, one sanitary block, dining and kitchen module, site office
Phased accommodation, two sanitary blocks, dining, laundry, first-aid room, administration, security
Further accommodation blocks added in later phases on a reserved layout
inputs: Beds per phase and shift ratio
Meals per shift and dining seats
Showers, toilets and laundry per bed
Site access, nearest port and road conditions
site_readiness: Level platform, drainage and access for trucks and a crane
Power, water and wastewater connection or the off-grid plant that replaces them
Foundation design from a site investigation

families.country_notes: Workforce accommodation rules — room size, occupancy, sanitation ratios, fire separation — differ by country and often by sector. MODUNERA does not describe any camp as compliant before a local engineer has checked it against the code that applies.
faq: Can you supply a complete camp?

A camp can be planned as accommodation, sanitary, dining and office modules with a site layout. Whether MODUNERA supplies the buildings only or also installation, and what remains with the operator or local contractors, is set in the proposal.
How fast can a camp be delivered?
That depends on quantities, specification, production slots and the transport route, and is stated in the proposal. No standard lead time is published.
Are the camps certified for mining sites?
No certification is claimed. Site-specific requirements — fire, HSE, occupancy — are reviewed with the client's engineers and local professionals for each project.

procurement_faq.title: Procurement FAQ for modular projects | MODUNERA
procurement_faq.description: Answers for procurement teams: supply models, EPC subcontracting, local installation, payment milestones, warranty, documents, lead times and what is not offered.
procurement_faq.lead: The questions procurement managers, contractors and developers ask before sending an RFQ — with the limits stated.
faq: Do you sell direct or through partners?
Both are possible: direct supply to the project owner, supply as a subcontract to an EPC or main contractor, or through a local distributor where one exists. The model is agreed per project.
Who installs the buildings?
MODUNERA's team, a local installation partner or the client's contractor, with supervision where agreed. The contract names who is responsible.
What payment milestones are usual?
Milestones are agreed per contract — typically linked to order, production stages and shipment. No standard terms are published.
What warranty applies?
Warranty terms are part of the contract and depend on the scope supplied and installed. They are stated in the proposal.
What documents can you provide?
Company registration data is published. A company profile, technical information and quality documents are supplied with a proposal. No certificate is claimed that does not exist.
What is the lead time?
It depends on quantities, specification, production slots and transport, and is stated in the proposal. No standard lead time is published.
Can you quote a price per square metre?
Not for project buildings. A price follows a brief, a specification and a delivery term.
Do you take part in public tenders?
Where the tender's eligibility rules allow. Send the reference and documents with your brief.
Do you handle permits?
No. Permits are applied for by the client or local professionals. MODUNERA supplies the technical documents the application needs, where agreed.
Can we visit the production?
Yes, by appointment. Ask for a visit in your enquiry.
Which countries do you deliver to?
MODUNERA sells tiny houses in Europe and assesses project enquiries from Europe and selected African markets case by case. No country is listed as served without a project.
Do you upload drawings through the website?
Not yet. Send drawings by e-mail after the first reply; the website does not store files.

quick.p: Seven fields. A person reads it and replies with the next step; the full project brief can follow.

fr_africa.h1: Solutions de bâtiments modulaires pour des projets en Afrique.
fr_africa.lead: Hébergement des équipes, logements préfabriqués ou bâtiments de chantier : présentez-nous votre projet. MODUNERA étudie les contraintes du site, les spécifications techniques et la logistique d'exportation au cas par cas.
fr_africa.answer: MODUNERA étudie des demandes de projets venant de marchés africains sélectionnés. Il n'existe à ce jour aucun projet MODUNERA livré en Afrique, et aucun pays n'est présenté comme desservi. Chaque projet passe d'abord par une étude de faisabilité : export, douane, autorisations locales, transport et partenaires sur place.
segments: Chantiers miniers, énergie, infrastructures — de 50 à 300 personnes et plus, par phases.
Programmes immobiliers, logements du personnel, logement social via un entrepreneur.
Bureaux, salles de réunion, blocs sanitaires, postes de garde.
Le bâtiment de salles de classe — l'agrément et l'exploitation restent à l'opérateur.
Postes de secours et petites cliniques — le bâtiment, pas l'activité médicale.
Unités d'hébergement et bâtiments communs, sans promesse de rendement.
